name: Université de Strasbourg
header:
Université de Strasbourg
France · Master Mathématiques et applications, parcours Mathématiques fondamentales (M1/M2); DU MARI and Mobil’ITI
scholarship; PhD through ED269
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Apply to the master first: the DU/scholarship application cannot replace degree admission.
• US EEF can close in January, well before the April Mobil’ITI deadline.
• The French-language master requires B2 French; an English UChicago degree is not a French exemption.
• M2 mathematics themes rotate; an AG-oriented 2027 curriculum is not yet verified.
• Mobil’ITI is a limited grant with tuition potentially additional, not a full-cost guarantee.
• Doctoral €1,300 net/month is an admission funding floor, not the amount promised by a contract.
• Faculty shortlist prioritizes AG, arithmetic, complex geometry and representation theory; individual 2027
availability is unverified. Emeriti are not presented as ordinary new supervisors.
• Yalkinoglu's official home-page bibliography stops at 2013, but primary 2025-2026 preprints and a 2026
institutional event establish recent activity; remove any assertion that no recent paper was found.
• Wach has publisher-verified 2023 p-adic Hodge research; a 2025 textbook is separate teaching output. No
2024-2026 research-paper evidence was verified.
• Lecomte's paper evidence is a 2023 preprint, not a 2024-2026 published article; preserve that date/status
distinction.
• Beliaeva's number-theory publication evidence remains old (2012). She is institutionally current and also
works in mathematics education, but should not be represented as a confirmed active 2027 number-theory
PhD supervisor without direct confirmation.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago mathematics BA can be assessed for M1 equivalence; M2 normally requires M1 or equivalent
advanced preparation, not an automatic four-year-BA entitlement. Master’s teaching is French. Doctorate
normally requires a research master’s, French grade at least 12/20 or approved exception; foreign-degree
equivalence needs ED approval. Direct BA-to-PhD eligibility is not established. International status is permitted;
F-1 confers no French immigration or EU fee status. [s1] [s2] [s8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Identify citizenship/residence route: US-resident non-EU candidates normally use Études en France (EEF),
whereas eligible EU applicants use MonMaster. Submit the exact mathematics master application before the
separate DU/Mobil’ITI form; that form requires its application number. For PhD, obtain an HDR supervisor’s
agreement, laboratory approval, research plan and funding before Amethis enrolment. [s2] [s6] [s8] [s12]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
For PhD, contact a relevant HDR-qualified supervisor and obtain the required interview/agreement before the
application. For master, admission is programme-based; M2 coordinators listed are Giuseppe Ancona and
Denis Villemonais. Faculty fit below does not confirm 2027 capacity or sole-supervision eligibility. M2 theme

changes annually: 2026-27 probability, 2024-25 algebra/topology, 2023-24 arithmetic/AG; 2027-28 theme
unknown. [s4] [s8] [s10] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use EEF/MonMaster/eCandidat according to the admission route; incorrect-channel files may not be reviewed.
DU survey requires the exact master application identifier, supports Resume Later, and is final only after
Submit. PhD: Amethis applicant file proceeds through supervisor, laboratory and ED validation before
administrative enrolment. [s2] [s6] [s8]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
2027-28 DU application and 30 April deadline explicit; US EEF 15 January 2027 explicit. M1/M2 local calendars
and 2027 doctoral competition are not published in checked sources. Faculty curriculum/tuition evidence still
refers to earlier academic years. [s2] [s5] [s6] [s8] [s12]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
US EEF HDAP fall 2027: 15 January 2027, 6 pm EST. Strasbourg’s 30 April 2027 EEF date is the university
review deadline, not the student submission deadline. Other 2027 master calendars are pending; faculty says
eCandidat dates will appear in February 2027. DU MARI: 30 April 2027, time/timezone unpublished. PhD 2027
competition dates are unpublished; prior 2026 applications closed 19 May. [s2] [s5] [s8] [s12]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Mobil’ITI: 30 April 2027, time/timezone not stated; separate from earlier master admission. Prior 2026
doctoral-contract cycle: project nomination 2 March at 16:00, candidate applications 19 May, interview 8-9
June, results 10-12 June; these are NOT 2027 deadlines. [s5] [s8]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
DU/Mobil’ITI requests at least two professor contacts and contacts them only if needed, so no universal
letter-upload deadline is published. PhD contract references accompany the competition dossier; 2027
deadline/count not established. EEF recommendations follow the relevant application checklist, not the DU
contact mechanism. [s6] [s8] [s12]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
French B2 evidence must satisfy the master application checklist; no separate 2027 language-score grace date
established. PhD requires French or English B2; test types and score-submission deadline are not specified in
the ED admission rules. [s2] [s8]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
Upload available academic results by the relevant application closing date; final degree proof is needed at
administrative registration. DU supporting uploads accompany the 30 April 2027 application. Foreign doctorate
equivalence and all Amethis documents must be accepted before registration; no 2027 blanket grace date
published. [s2] [s5] [s8]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Offers must be confirmed; route-specific 2027 response dates are not yet established. Prior PhD 2026
enrolment ran 26 June-30 September for an October start. Do not substitute this for a 2027 commitment
deadline or assume a US April 15 rule. [s2] [s8]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
DU/Mobil’ITI: at least TWO professor contact details; this is not a requirement to upload two letters initially. EEF
broadly recommends one or two references, but the mathematics master’s mandatory count is not publicly
established. Doctoral-contract dossier asks recommendations without a fixed published count. [s6] [s8] [s12]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI uses the DU’s professor contacts plus a signed scholarship request form. No independent scholarship
referee essay/questions are publicly specified. Doctoral supervisors/laboratory provide required formal
endorsements distinct from ordinary recommendations. [s6] [s8]
What sends the invitation [2027 confirmed]
DU form explicitly says professor contacts are NOT automatically notified: organisers contact them only if
needed for evaluation. Master EEF and doctoral reference invitation mechanics are not established. [s6]
Before versus after submission [2027 confirmed]
DU: no automatic invitation at entry or submission; conditional later contact only. No public evidence
establishes an after-submission invitation rule for the academic master/PhD route. [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
No public applicant-facing referee receipt confirmation rule found for DU/EEF/PhD. DU has no routine initial
letter upload; do not interpret application submission confirmation as referee receipt. [s6] [s8] [s14]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
DU answers can be edited before clicking Submit and saved with Resume Later. Reference replacement, letter
updating and reuse after submission are unpublished; EEF/PhD reuse rules also unresolved. [s6] [s14]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required for DU and PhD; upload CV. Faculty advice (paraphrase): identify institutions, degree titles,
cities/countries, explain abbreviations and account for every year including gaps/repeats. PhD CV covers
results/honours from the last secondary-school year. No page/font limit found. DU upload: one file, maximum
10 MB. [s3] [s5] [s6] [s8]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Master motivation advice (paraphrase): explain course/institution changes and concrete reasons for this
programme and its courses. EEF motivation text maximum 2,500 characters, in French for French-taught
programmes. DU motivation letter required; one upload, 10 MB maximum, no published word/page/font limit.
[s3] [s6] [s12]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
No standalone personal/background essay identified in public master/DU/doctoral lists; do not invent an
optional attachment. Relevant circumstances can be explained within requested CV/motivation material. [s3]
[s5] [s8]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
M2 motivation should address the particular annual research theme. DU selection weighs motivation for
interdisciplinary activities. Doctoral interests belong in the proposal and motivation letter; no separate
research-interest essay specified. Limits beyond the proposal are unpublished. [s1] [s5] [s8]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
Master/DU: not listed as a separate required document. PhD: required 1-2 page proposal describing the
question, brief state of the art/references, initial work plan and resources (paraphrase); upload through
Amethis. Font/margins not published. [s6] [s8]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Doctoral admission explicitly requests the master’s thesis. No writing sample/thesis requirement found for
master/DU; unsolicited-paper upload permission is unverified. Thesis format/size limits are not public. [s6] [s8]
Publications list [Unresolved]
No standalone publication list or paper uploads requested in checked master/DU/PhD lists. Research outputs
can be described in the required CV if relevant; no verified extra-upload or URL-only policy. [s3] [s6] [s8]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course essay/template published; academic records supply courses, and M2 fit
belongs in motivation. No length or additional upload permission established. [s1] [s6]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
Mobil’ITI: tick the scholarship request and upload its signed/dated form in addition to DU CV, motivation and
transcripts. The linked DOCX could not be inspected; exact questions/format remain unresolved. No published
additional essay length. Doctoral contract competition separately requires motivation, information form and
supervisor interview certificate. [s5] [s6] [s8]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
DU transcript upload permits 1-6 files, each up to 10 MB. PhD additionally requires signed doctoral charter,
training agreement, supervisor/lab opinions, interview certificate, funding duration/amount and coverage;
foreign degree approval where relevant. No public uniform font or file-size rules for PhD. [s6] [s8]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI: €7,000 net over 10 months (€700/month). Eligible incoming students may receive €500 installation
plus travel reimbursement up to €2,000 when travel exceeds 4,000 km, or €1,000 below that distance;
maximum €9,500. Existing Strasbourg higher-education students do not receive travel/installation benefits.
ED269 requires funding at least €1,300 net/month for the full PhD: an eligibility floor, NOT a scholarship offer.
[s6] [s7] [s8]
Years of support [Conflict]
Master award initially one academic year/10 months. Current 2027-28 form allows conditional renewal for 6-10
months; older scholarship page says up to 6 months, so obtain a written renewal term. Doctoral contracts
normally fund 3 years; extension possibilities do not guarantee a fourth year. [s6] [s7] [s9]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI is open to eligible international applicants selected for an associated master and DU; geography
affects relocation benefits, not automatic entitlement. Doctoral foreign degrees need equivalence and a funded
supervisor/project. Citizenship-specific external scholarship eligibility must be checked separately. [s5] [s7] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI requires completion of the complementary DU; 80% paid after arrival certification and 20% at
completion, with possible recovery if abandoned. Income-based grant combination is allowed; specified Unistra
mobility, Erasmus and other IdEx awards cannot normally be combined for the same year. Tuition is not stated
as automatically covered. [s6] [s7]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
A master admission application alone does not apply for Mobil’ITI: submit DU form and scholarship request by
its deadline. Admission to DU precedes scholarship assessment; possible interview in summer 2027. Doctoral
contract awards require the separate annual competition or project application. [s5] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
PhD funding can arise through university, regional, CNRS and project contracts; CIFRE/other named schemes
depend on individual eligibility and project. No universal master stipend or automatic funded PhD offer is
published. Optional doctoral teaching duties are contract-specific. [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
Campus France USA full admissions processing US$460; already-admitted pre-consular processing US$270 is a
different route. No separate mathematics application fee established. Current form gives PRIOR 2026-27
master registration €255 for listed exempt/national-fee groups versus €3,950 for other international students,
plus DU €167; 2027-28 rates/CVEC not established. These are tuition/registration, not application fees. [s6] [s13]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
No automatic UChicago/F-1 application-fee waiver established. Nationality/residence and scholarship
exemptions affect differentiated tuition; obtain a specific university decision rather than assuming Mobil’ITI
pays or waives it. Campus France exemptions must be assessed under its own fee policy. [s6] [s13]

Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Giuseppe Ancona
Motives, algebraic cycles, Hodge and Lefschetz standard conjectures; arithmetic geometry. [s10] [s20]

Professor. Taking new students in 2027 not confirmed.

Official institution/faculty publication metadata supporting this research match.
Rutger Noot
Arithmetic geometry of abelian and Shimura varieties; Galois representations, Frobenius classes, Hodge/Tate
classes and p-adic/Weil-Deligne representations. [s10] [s29] [euqb32] [euqb33]
Listed as professor on the current IRMA arithmetic and algebraic geometry roster; no retirement claim follows from the old paper
list.
Research evidence: 2017; older evidence, not a recent-paper claim · The p-adic representation of the Weil-Deligne group
associated to an abelian variety
Official institution/faculty publication metadata supporting this research match.
Research evidence: 2017 · The p-adic representation of the Weil-Deligne group associated to an abelian variety
Journal of Number Theory 172, 301-320. The official page itself was last updated 25 April 2017; this is explicitly older evidence.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier research description: Abelian varieties, Galois representations and Shimura/Mumford-Tate theory.
Earlier appointment description: Professor; recent official paper metadata not found; latest listed research paper is 2017.
Taking new students in 2027 not confirmed.
Final verification: No 2023-2026 paper verified after targeted searches and the official list check. Ask for current projects
and 2027 supervision availability; do not present 2017 as recent.
Florence Lecomte
Motives and their realizations, algebraic K-theory, unipotent/fundamental-group constructions and their
relationship with homology; the 2023 Enriquez joint paper connects relative singular homology with
fundamental-group-algebra quotients. [s10] [euqa1] [euqa13] [euqa14]

supervision/HDR status and 2027 availability require confirmation.
Research evidence: 2023 preprint · Natural transformations relating homotopy and singular homology functors
With Benjamin Enriquez; independently listed by the official CNRS AHGT network as RIMS preprint 1978. No later 2024-2026
research paper verified.

[s30]

Official institution/faculty publication metadata supporting this research match.

CNRS chargé de recherche. Taking new students in 2027 not confirmed.

Official institution/faculty publication metadata supporting this research match.
Tatiana Beliaeva
Older verified research concerns Iwasawa theory, cyclotomic units, Gauss sums and Galois cohomology.
Current official INSPÉ profile also identifies mathematics didactics; confirm whether active number-theory
doctoral supervision is available. [s10] [euqa1] [euqa15] [euqa16] [euqa17] [euqa18] [euqa19]
Current Strasbourg maîtresse de conférences, listed by IRMA and INSPÉ; June 2025 university programme confirms IRMA/INSPÉ
activity. The UCLy economist of the same name is a different person and her AI/business papers must not be attributed here.
Research evidence: 2012 · Indices isotypiques des éléments cyclotomiques
With Jean-Robert Belliard; coauthor's official CNRS page confirms Tokyo J. Math. 35(1),139-164 (2012). Older subject evidence
only; no 2024-2026 relevant research paper verified.
Nathalie Wach
p-adic Hodge theory, crystalline/Galois representations, filtered phi-modules and (phi,Gamma)-modules;
additional mathematics-education work. The 2023 article studies crystalline interpretation of the Deligne-Illusie
isomorphism. [s10] [euqa1] [euqa10] [euqa11] [euqa12]
Current Strasbourg maîtresse de conférences on the IRMA AGA roster and current IREM director on the university's journal page.
Ask about doctoral supervision/HDR status and 2027 availability.
Research evidence: 2023 · Interprétation cristalline de l’isomorphisme de Deligne-Illusie
With Christine Huyghe; AIF 73(3),1133-1201. The old coauthor page says a 2017 preprint, but the publisher confirms final
publication in 2023. No 2024-2026 relevant research article was verified.

Quantum affine algebras, cluster algebras, friezes and representation-theoretic combinatorics. [s11] [s35]

text:
Université de Strasbourg
France · Master Mathématiques et applications, parcours Mathématiques fondamentales (M1/M2); DU MARI and Mobil’ITI
scholarship; PhD through ED269
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Apply to the master first: the DU/scholarship application cannot replace degree admission.
• US EEF can close in January, well before the April Mobil’ITI deadline.
• The French-language master requires B2 French; an English UChicago degree is not a French exemption.
• M2 mathematics themes rotate; an AG-oriented 2027 curriculum is not yet verified.
• Mobil’ITI is a limited grant with tuition potentially additional, not a full-cost guarantee.
• Doctoral €1,300 net/month is an admission funding floor, not the amount promised by a contract.
• Faculty shortlist prioritizes AG, arithmetic, complex geometry and representation theory; individual 2027
availability is unverified. Emeriti are not presented as ordinary new supervisors.
• Yalkinoglu's official home-page bibliography stops at 2013, but primary 2025-2026 preprints and a 2026
institutional event establish recent activity; remove any assertion that no recent paper was found.
• Wach has publisher-verified 2023 p-adic Hodge research; a 2025 textbook is separate teaching output. No
2024-2026 research-paper evidence was verified.
• Lecomte's paper evidence is a 2023 preprint, not a 2024-2026 published article; preserve that date/status
distinction.
• Beliaeva's number-theory publication evidence remains old (2012). She is institutionally current and also
works in mathematics education, but should not be represented as a confirmed active 2027 number-theory
PhD supervisor without direct confirmation.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago mathematics BA can be assessed for M1 equivalence; M2 normally requires M1 or equivalent
advanced preparation, not an automatic four-year-BA entitlement. Master’s teaching is French. Doctorate
normally requires a research master’s, French grade at least 12/20 or approved exception; foreign-degree
equivalence needs ED approval. Direct BA-to-PhD eligibility is not established. International status is permitted;
F-1 confers no French immigration or EU fee status. [s1] [s2] [s8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Identify citizenship/residence route: US-resident non-EU candidates normally use Études en France (EEF),
whereas eligible EU applicants use MonMaster. Submit the exact mathematics master application before the
separate DU/Mobil’ITI form; that form requires its application number. For PhD, obtain an HDR supervisor’s
agreement, laboratory approval, research plan and funding before Amethis enrolment. [s2] [s6] [s8] [s12]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
For PhD, contact a relevant HDR-qualified supervisor and obtain the required interview/agreement before the
application. For master, admission is programme-based; M2 coordinators listed are Giuseppe Ancona and
Denis Villemonais. Faculty fit below does not confirm 2027 capacity or sole-supervision eligibility. M2 theme

changes annually: 2026-27 probability, 2024-25 algebra/topology, 2023-24 arithmetic/AG; 2027-28 theme
unknown. [s4] [s8] [s10] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use EEF/MonMaster/eCandidat according to the admission route; incorrect-channel files may not be reviewed.
DU survey requires the exact master application identifier, supports Resume Later, and is final only after
Submit. PhD: Amethis applicant file proceeds through supervisor, laboratory and ED validation before
administrative enrolment. [s2] [s6] [s8]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
2027-28 DU application and 30 April deadline explicit; US EEF 15 January 2027 explicit. M1/M2 local calendars
and 2027 doctoral competition are not published in checked sources. Faculty curriculum/tuition evidence still
refers to earlier academic years. [s2] [s5] [s6] [s8] [s12]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
US EEF HDAP fall 2027: 15 January 2027, 6 pm EST. Strasbourg’s 30 April 2027 EEF date is the university
review deadline, not the student submission deadline. Other 2027 master calendars are pending; faculty says
eCandidat dates will appear in February 2027. DU MARI: 30 April 2027, time/timezone unpublished. PhD 2027
competition dates are unpublished; prior 2026 applications closed 19 May. [s2] [s5] [s8] [s12]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Mobil’ITI: 30 April 2027, time/timezone not stated; separate from earlier master admission. Prior 2026
doctoral-contract cycle: project nomination 2 March at 16:00, candidate applications 19 May, interview 8-9
June, results 10-12 June; these are NOT 2027 deadlines. [s5] [s8]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
DU/Mobil’ITI requests at least two professor contacts and contacts them only if needed, so no universal
letter-upload deadline is published. PhD contract references accompany the competition dossier; 2027
deadline/count not established. EEF recommendations follow the relevant application checklist, not the DU
contact mechanism. [s6] [s8] [s12]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
French B2 evidence must satisfy the master application checklist; no separate 2027 language-score grace date
established. PhD requires French or English B2; test types and score-submission deadline are not specified in
the ED admission rules. [s2] [s8]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
Upload available academic results by the relevant application closing date; final degree proof is needed at
administrative registration. DU supporting uploads accompany the 30 April 2027 application. Foreign doctorate
equivalence and all Amethis documents must be accepted before registration; no 2027 blanket grace date
published. [s2] [s5] [s8]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Offers must be confirmed; route-specific 2027 response dates are not yet established. Prior PhD 2026
enrolment ran 26 June-30 September for an October start. Do not substitute this for a 2027 commitment
deadline or assume a US April 15 rule. [s2] [s8]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Master: French B2, not an English-medium programme. ED269 doctorate: French OR English B2. No
IELTS/TOEFL minimum or specific English test mandate was found in the checked mathematics/ED pages. [s1]
[s2] [s8]

UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
An English-medium UChicago degree does not establish French B2 or a master French-test exemption. For PhD,
whether the degree itself documents English B2 needs ED confirmation; no automatic UChicago-specific waiver
is published. [s2] [s8]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not listed in the checked master, DU or doctoral requirements; no published requirement or invitation to
upload GRE scores was found. Treat as not requested on those checklists, not a verified prohibition. [s1] [s6] [s8]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Master: transcripts supporting prerequisite/equivalence assessment, available results before close, final
diploma at registration. DU: last three academic years’ transcripts. PhD: master grades/equivalence, thesis,
foreign-degree exemption where applicable and funding proof; contract competition also asks relative class
rank and final master results when available. [s1] [s2] [s5] [s8]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
No separate standardized mathematics-course list found. Transcripts must establish algebra, real/complex
analysis, measure, topology and probability preparation; M2 applicants should explain preparation for the
year’s theme. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No universal course-description attachment or format found on public master/DU pages. Equivalence assessors
may need clarification of UChicago content; obtain instructions before treating a syllabus packet as required or
accepted. [s1] [s6]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
DU/Mobil’ITI: at least TWO professor contact details; this is not a requirement to upload two letters initially. EEF
broadly recommends one or two references, but the mathematics master’s mandatory count is not publicly
established. Doctoral-contract dossier asks recommendations without a fixed published count. [s6] [s8] [s12]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI uses the DU’s professor contacts plus a signed scholarship request form. No independent scholarship
referee essay/questions are publicly specified. Doctoral supervisors/laboratory provide required formal
endorsements distinct from ordinary recommendations. [s6] [s8]
What sends the invitation [2027 confirmed]
DU form explicitly says professor contacts are NOT automatically notified: organisers contact them only if
needed for evaluation. Master EEF and doctoral reference invitation mechanics are not established. [s6]
Before versus after submission [2027 confirmed]
DU: no automatic invitation at entry or submission; conditional later contact only. No public evidence
establishes an after-submission invitation rule for the academic master/PhD route. [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
No public applicant-facing referee receipt confirmation rule found for DU/EEF/PhD. DU has no routine initial
letter upload; do not interpret application submission confirmation as referee receipt. [s6] [s8] [s14]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
DU answers can be edited before clicking Submit and saved with Resume Later. Reference replacement, letter
updating and reuse after submission are unpublished; EEF/PhD reuse rules also unresolved. [s6] [s14]

Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required for DU and PhD; upload CV. Faculty advice (paraphrase): identify institutions, degree titles,
cities/countries, explain abbreviations and account for every year including gaps/repeats. PhD CV covers
results/honours from the last secondary-school year. No page/font limit found. DU upload: one file, maximum
10 MB. [s3] [s5] [s6] [s8]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Master motivation advice (paraphrase): explain course/institution changes and concrete reasons for this
programme and its courses. EEF motivation text maximum 2,500 characters, in French for French-taught
programmes. DU motivation letter required; one upload, 10 MB maximum, no published word/page/font limit.
[s3] [s6] [s12]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
No standalone personal/background essay identified in public master/DU/doctoral lists; do not invent an
optional attachment. Relevant circumstances can be explained within requested CV/motivation material. [s3]
[s5] [s8]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
M2 motivation should address the particular annual research theme. DU selection weighs motivation for
interdisciplinary activities. Doctoral interests belong in the proposal and motivation letter; no separate
research-interest essay specified. Limits beyond the proposal are unpublished. [s1] [s5] [s8]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
Master/DU: not listed as a separate required document. PhD: required 1-2 page proposal describing the
question, brief state of the art/references, initial work plan and resources (paraphrase); upload through
Amethis. Font/margins not published. [s6] [s8]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Doctoral admission explicitly requests the master’s thesis. No writing sample/thesis requirement found for
master/DU; unsolicited-paper upload permission is unverified. Thesis format/size limits are not public. [s6] [s8]
Publications list [Unresolved]
No standalone publication list or paper uploads requested in checked master/DU/PhD lists. Research outputs
can be described in the required CV if relevant; no verified extra-upload or URL-only policy. [s3] [s6] [s8]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course essay/template published; academic records supply courses, and M2 fit
belongs in motivation. No length or additional upload permission established. [s1] [s6]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
Mobil’ITI: tick the scholarship request and upload its signed/dated form in addition to DU CV, motivation and
transcripts. The linked DOCX could not be inspected; exact questions/format remain unresolved. No published
additional essay length. Doctoral contract competition separately requires motivation, information form and
supervisor interview certificate. [s5] [s6] [s8]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
DU transcript upload permits 1-6 files, each up to 10 MB. PhD additionally requires signed doctoral charter,
training agreement, supervisor/lab opinions, interview certificate, funding duration/amount and coverage;
foreign degree approval where relevant. No public uniform font or file-size rules for PhD. [s6] [s8]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI: €7,000 net over 10 months (€700/month). Eligible incoming students may receive €500 installation
plus travel reimbursement up to €2,000 when travel exceeds 4,000 km, or €1,000 below that distance;
maximum €9,500. Existing Strasbourg higher-education students do not receive travel/installation benefits.
ED269 requires funding at least €1,300 net/month for the full PhD: an eligibility floor, NOT a scholarship offer.
[s6] [s7] [s8]
Years of support [Conflict]
Master award initially one academic year/10 months. Current 2027-28 form allows conditional renewal for 6-10
months; older scholarship page says up to 6 months, so obtain a written renewal term. Doctoral contracts
normally fund 3 years; extension possibilities do not guarantee a fourth year. [s6] [s7] [s9]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI is open to eligible international applicants selected for an associated master and DU; geography
affects relocation benefits, not automatic entitlement. Doctoral foreign degrees need equivalence and a funded
supervisor/project. Citizenship-specific external scholarship eligibility must be checked separately. [s5] [s7] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Mobil’ITI requires completion of the complementary DU; 80% paid after arrival certification and 20% at
completion, with possible recovery if abandoned. Income-based grant combination is allowed; specified Unistra
mobility, Erasmus and other IdEx awards cannot normally be combined for the same year. Tuition is not stated
as automatically covered. [s6] [s7]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
A master admission application alone does not apply for Mobil’ITI: submit DU form and scholarship request by
its deadline. Admission to DU precedes scholarship assessment; possible interview in summer 2027. Doctoral
contract awards require the separate annual competition or project application. [s5] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
PhD funding can arise through university, regional, CNRS and project contracts; CIFRE/other named schemes
depend on individual eligibility and project. No universal master stipend or automatic funded PhD offer is
published. Optional doctoral teaching duties are contract-specific. [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
Campus France USA full admissions processing US$460; already-admitted pre-consular processing US$270 is a
